content: 1. The WHO-4 symptom screen and chest X-ray (CXR) are used to identify abnormalities indicative of active tuberculosis (TB). However, false positives (FPs) can occur, leading to patients being incorrectly classified as having active TB. The number of FPs varies depending on the diagnostic method used. 2. Studies included in the analysis were determined to have a low risk of bias, and no downgrades were applied for indirectness. However, specificity estimates showed inconsistency, ranging from 2% to 60%, with non-overlapping confidence intervals, leading to a downgrade for inconsistency. 3. The radiation dose from a single CXR is approximately 1 mSv, which is one-third of the average annual environmental radiation dose (3 mSv) and one-tenth of the annual accepted dose for the general public. This dose is comparable to or less than the radiation exposure from a round-trip intercontinental flight. The risk of tissue reactions or cancer from this low radiation dose is minimal but not negligible, as a linear no-threshold model assumes even low doses increase cancer risk slightly. 4. CXRs can detect other lung diseases beyond TB, providing an indirect benefit by identifying other morbidities that may require medical attention. This aligns with a practical approach to lung health. 5. The certainty of evidence regarding the effects of CXR as a diagnostic tool is moderate. While the radiation risk is low, the direct benefits include identifying more TB cases and other diseases. However, there may be additional burdens on people living with HIV (PLHIV) to access CXR unless mobile units are available. 6. WHO-recommended molecular diagnostics, such as Xpert® MTB/RIF and Xpert® MTB/RIF Ultra, are the initial diagnostic tests for TB in PLHIV. The Ultra assay has a 7% higher sensitivity than Xpert® MTB/RIF. Lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan (LF-LAM) is also recommended for PLHIV, with sensitivity increasing as HIV disease progresses. 7. Early initiation of antiretroviral therapy (ART) in PLHIV reduces mortality and TB transmission, simplifies programmatic demands, and improves health outcomes. Undetected TB or delays in diagnosis are associated with increased mortality and transmission. 8. CXR infrastructure is not yet decentralized in many resource-limited settings, which limits access for individuals outside district or national centers. This can result in high costs and time burdens for patients. However, advancements in digital technology and mobile CXR units are expanding access. 9. The cost-effectiveness of CXR following WHO-4 symptom screening has been demonstrated in several studies. For example, in South Africa, the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) was $360 per additional TB case diagnosed. In Russia, mass CXR screening with mobile units was cost-effective with an ICER of $549 per additional TB case diagnosed. 10. The use of CXR in combination with WHO-4 symptom screening is more sensitive than symptom screening alone, leading to more individuals requiring diagnostic confirmation. While this increases costs, it also identifies more TB cases, reducing disease burden and mortality. 11. Equity concerns arise due to limited access to CXR in lowand middle-income countries. Decentralization and investment in infrastructure are needed to improve access. Mobile CXR units and reduced machine costs can help address these disparities. 12. Acceptability of CXR as a diagnostic tool may be influenced by perceived and enacted stigma related to HIV and TB. Limited qualitative evidence exists, but stigma may complicate decision-making for PLHIV. 13. Feasibility of implementing CXR depends on infrastructure and human resources. In high TB burden settings, lack of infrastructure and trained personnel limits availability. However, systematic screening with mobile digital X-ray services has been shown to be feasible and scalable when integrated into national programs. 14. CXR is also used for purposes beyond TB detection, which may enhance its utility in healthcare systems. However, investment in infrastructure and human resources is necessary to make it widely feasible in resource-limited settings.
